the inhibitory Smad7 and the Smad6 proteins promote differentiation of ciliated cells from embryonic stem (Es) cells.
inhibitory Smads, Smad7, and Smad6 specifically promote the differentiation of ES cells into ciliated ependymal cells, but not into ciliated neural cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differentiation of ciliated cells from mouse ES cells and the role of Smad proteins in this process.
the identification of a novel role for inhibitory Smad signaling in the regulation of the differentiation and subtype specification of cilia in mouse ES cells.
the role of Smad proteins in the differentiation of ciliated cells from mouse ES cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inhibitory Smads promote ciliated cell differentiation from mouse ES cell, and that these Smads are involved in subtype specification of cilia.
the inhibitory Smads are necessary for the differentiation of mouse ES cells into ependyman-like ciliated cells.
Smad6/7 promotes the differentiation of mouse ES cells into a specific subtype of ciliated cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inhibitory Smads promote the differentiation of ES cells into ciliated ependymal cells, but not into motile cilia cells.
inhibitory Smads are involved in the regulation of ciliogenesis and ciliogenesis-related cell fate specification during the differentiation of embryonic stem cells.
Smad7 and 6 promote ciliated cell differentiation and subtype specification from embryonic stem cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Smad proteins are involved in the regulation of cilia formation.
Smad7 and 6 are important regulators for the differentiation of mouse ES cells into ciliated cell types.
Smad7 and/or Smad6 are necessary and sufficient to induce the differentiation of mouse ES cells into ciliated ependymal cells.
